source_candidate.claim_family: SLoRA active-state versus archive-state and reconstruction-cost accounting

mechanical_findings.finding: Before task t>1, the released SLoRA-Pre trainer starts from the base model, iterates every prior order directory, loads each prior max.safetensors, and merges that denoised LoRA into the model with merge_and_unload before creating one fresh LoRA for the current task.
mechanical_findings.consequence: Current trainable adapter count is constant with task count, but startup/reconstruction performs one historical-delta replay per prior task.

mechanical_findings.finding: The released evaluation builder similarly resolves all order* directories and sequentially loads/merges each denoised task delta before evaluation. There is no inference router or active historical adapter bank in this path.
mechanical_findings.consequence: Deployed in-memory active routing state can be constant, while released reconstruction I/O and merge work grow approximately linearly in the number of retained task deltas.

mechanical_findings.finding: Each training order directory retains adapter_model.safetensors and additionally writes max.safetensors after denoising. The top-level training launcher uses eight tasks and LoRA rank 64 over q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, up_proj, gate_proj and down_proj for Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct.
mechanical_findings.consequence: The experiment's retained archive is not constant-size even though only one new LoRA is trainable at a time.

mechanical_findings.finding: The pinned repository contains no first-class training/evaluation path that serializes the fully merged continual model into a compact replacement checkpoint and then discards prior order directories. All public continual train/eval paths inspected reconstruct by replaying order directories.
mechanical_findings.consequence: A compacted merged checkpoint is not a supported public lifecycle contract at this commit. A user could in principle add a full-model save after merge, but that is an untested adaptation and would trade the delta archive for a full backbone checkpoint rather than demonstrating a compact retained continual delta.

parameter_accounting.released_example: Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct, rank 64, 32 layers, hidden size 4096, intermediate size 14336, 8 KV heads / 32 attention heads; seven target projections per layer.
parameter_accounting.raw_lora_formula: per linear module r*(in_dim+out_dim); sum over q,k,v,o,up,gate,down and all 32 layers
parameter_accounting.scope_note: This is a parameter/tensor-payload calculation for the released example configuration, excluding safetensors metadata, configs, trainer/checkpoint state and the additional denoised max.safetensors files. The denoised file has adaptive per-module rank selected from candidate fractions and therefore requires actual run artifacts for an exact byte count.

verdict.summary: The sealed worker's lifecycle distinction is supported. SLoRA's active trainable adapter and inference routing state need not grow with T, but the released reproducibility archive and the startup/evaluation reconstruction path do grow with T. For the public eight-task Llama-3-8B example, raw rank-64 adapter tensor payload alone is nominally about 320 MiB per task, or 2.5 GiB across eight task directories, before counting denoised copies and other files.
scope_corrections: Do not describe SLoRA as constant-storage without specifying deployed active state versus retained experiment/archive state.
Do not describe the 2.5 GiB calculation as measured repository artifact bytes; it is a mechanically derived tensor-payload figure under the released example architecture/configuration.

Do not claim the method fundamentally requires replaying all task deltas forever. This audit establishes that the pinned public scripts do so and do not expose a supported compacted replacement path; a new implementation could change that lifecycle.
Do not count merge-and-unload as an inference router. It reconstructs one merged model before use.

next_verification: Inspect the sealed FLEX claim from the same continual-learning artifact: pin the official RINC-CL/FLEX implementation and determine exactly what task-boundary information, fingerprint normalization, router calibration data, and task-correlated metadata are available at training and evaluation.
